thread:
maria: Heads-up - we discovered a 6h gap in agg_hours (eu) for 2026-03-20. Planning a targeted backfill tonight at 02:00 UTC. Need to decide queue affinity so it doesn't starve realtime recomputes. :eyes:
aj: +1 to low-priority pool with aggressive preemption. Can we route by tenant priority so prod-critical tenants aren't preempted?
kevin: We have fairshare tokens but they're global. Could add a backfill-affinity tag so scheduler prefers GPUs with spare capacity.
linh: If we tag nodes, KV cache warm-up could spike memory. Backfills should run with smaller batch sizes and avoid KV warmups where possible.
maria: Agreed. Also want a dry-run to estimate GPU-hours, ETA and cost. Console should surface estimated token-hours before kickoff.
sam: For dry-run we can simulate last-week traffic for a micro-window and produce a sample artifact. Suggest CLI flag --dry-run to emit estimates + sample.
kevin: Proposed CLI:
```
ri backfill create --target=agg_hours --range=2026-03-20..2026-03-20 \\
  --queue=backfill-lowprio --dry-run --canary=0.01
```
kevin: Dry-run output should include: estimated GPU-hours, affected tenants list, sample rows, dedupe-rate estimate.
linh: Concerning dedupe: late rows overlapping primary ingest risk double-counting. Need idempotent upsert keys and TTL reconciliation. Add a preflight check to verify idempotency keys exist.
nancy: Console could show a "preflight passed/failed" badge and link to the sample artifact to cut down ops handoffs.
aj: Also routing fallback: if lowprio saturates, route to dedicated nodes with strict per-tenant rate-limits rather than spilling into realtime. That keeps SLAs intact.
maria: Plan for tonight: run dry-run 22:00 UTC, review by 23:00, manual approve for 02:00 start. Who can own the dry-run?
kevin: I'll run the dry-run and post results. Ops-bot, please schedule a pagerless window 02:00-05:00 for fallback lanes.
ops-bot: scheduled maintenance window: telemetry-backfill-eu 02:00-05:00 UTC — notifications sent to #eng-oncall.
sam: UX ask — include "expected budget burn" in the backfill modal pulled from the dry-run artifact.
maria: We'll need a canary: 1% tenants first, validate aggregates with console diff. Abort if diffs > 0.5%.
linh: I'll add an automated diff job that compares canary output to baseline and emits pass/fail.
kevin: Dry-run started; uploading sample artifact to s3://ri-backfill/dryruns/4812345678.json
kevin: Dry-run results: est 1.3 GPU-hours, est cost $28, dedupe ~0.2%, ETA for full run ~2h at assigned slots. Artifact: s3://ri-backfill/dryruns/4812345678.json
maria: Thanks. Approve manual kickoff if no objections by 00:30 UTC. React :thumbsup: to approve.
nancy: Added console precheck flag and UI note about canary thresholds. Also linked sample artifact in modal.
aj: Ops note — ensure model kernels for realtime aren't evicted. Apply node-affinity label `backfill=true` only to spare nodes.
maria: Great coordination, thanks all. Will post run decision at 00:30.
kevin: standing by to launch.
nancy: I'll add the console banner and canary progress chart.
kevin: launched canary at 02:00 UTC (0.5% tenants).
ops-bot: job telemetry-backfill-eu-canary started (job_id: tb-4812345678-canary).
kevin: canary diff = 0.03% (within threshold). progressing to 10% after 15m.
maria: If thresholds exceeded abort and tag incident backfill-rollback.
kevin: canary passed; escalating to full window. starting bulk with queue backfill-lowprio and affinity label backfill=true.
ops-bot: job telemetry-backfill-eu started (job_id: tb-4812345678-bulk). estimated finish 04:15 UTC.
sam: Console shows estimated budget burn ~$2k if full run completes — FYI finance.
maria: Add postmortem checklist to consider smaller default batch size for EU during business hours.
kevin: Job finished 03:58 UTC. final diff 0.04%. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
